subject: Azure Marketplace: incorrect credit allocations and VAT on Aug invoices
messages:
From: Contoso Finance <contoso-finops@contoso.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Azure Marketplace Billing <azure-marketplace-billing@microsoft.com>
Date: Mon, 10 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Discrepancy: VAT charged and credits applied to wrong invoice

Hi Neha,

We noticed on our August Azure Marketplace statement that a set of marketplace credits Redwood issued (ref: INV-2026-08-01-AZ-Contoso) landed as a single line-level credit on invoice 2026-08-01 instead of being apportioned across subscription usage lines. This caused our tax/VAT calculation to be off and triggered a potential reclaim in our downstream reports.

Quick summary: 
- Total credits expected to reduce Gross Charges: USD 12,450
- Credits appear as single negative line on invoice 2026-08-01 (see attached stub)
- VAT/Tax was still calculated on the pre-credit gross for several line items; Contoso owes an adjustment entry on their accounting side unless invoices are reissued.

Can Redwood confirm whether the credits were submitted to Azure as a single settlement credit, or whether they sent line-level credit mapping? If this was an Azure-side allocation issue, please can you open a seller support case asap and loop us in — our accounting cutoff is 8/15. We can share the exact GL-level mapping if helpful.

Thanks,
Elena Martinez
Contoso Finance — Marketplace Billing
contoso-finops@contoso.com

Attachment: INV-2026-08-01-AZ-Contoso.pdf (invoice stub)
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Contoso Finance <contoso-finops@contoso.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Azure Marketplace Billing <azure-marketplace-billing@microsoft.com>
Date: Mon, 10 Aug 2026 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Discrepancy: VAT charged and credits applied to wrong invoice

Hi Elena — thanks for flagging this and sharing the stub. Sorry for the disruption.

Short answers up front: we (Redwood) issued credits back to Azure on 2026-08-02 as part of our marketplace settlement pass, but we did not control how the Marketplace portal apportioned those credits across line items on the buyer invoice. We'll open a ticket with Azure Seller Support to ask for either: (A) reissue of the invoice with credits apportioned per usage line, or (B) issuance of a credit note and corrected VAT calculation.

Next steps I am initiating: 
- Marcus will pull our settlement extract and attach a CSV matching Contoso's subscription/usage IDs.
- Marissa: can you confirm Redwood's accounting view of the original settlement (date / settlement id) so we can include that in support case?
- I'll open the Azure case and demand timeline for reissuance before Contoso's 8/15 cutoff; will include Contoso on the threads.

@Contoso: any GL mapping you can share now would speed this up.

Regards,
Neha Kapoor
Head of Partnerships, Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwood.ai

--

Team,

I've pulled the settlement/ledger extract for the Aug 2 settlement run and attached aug-billing-extract.csv. Key notes:
- Settlement ID: S-2026-08-02-7743 (internal)
- Gross marketplace charge reported to Azure for Contoso: USD 124,500
- Credit issued as part of settlement: USD 12,450 (credit reference CR-7743)
- Our mapping shows credits tied to three subscription IDs (sub_8941, sub_8942, sub_8943) with line-level usage.

It looks like our payload to Azure included per-subscription credit metadata, so this may be an Azure allocation/rendering problem.

Planned actions: 
1) I'll open a Seller Support case with Microsoft and attach the CSV + invoice stub + our settlement proof.
2) If Azure's response is delayed, Neha — recommend offering Contoso a temporary journal/credit memo from Redwood to avoid their bookkeeping impact; we can reverse upon reissued invoices.

Hello Azure Seller Support team,

We're opening a formal support request (please see attachments) on behalf of Contoso Ltd. — credits Redwood issued in the Aug 2 settlement run (CR-7743) are reflected as a single negative line on the buyer invoice instead of being apportioned across the buyer's subscription usage lines, which leads to incorrect VAT calculations. Full details below and attached:
- Our settlement extract (aug-billing-extract.csv) with subscription-level credit mappings
- Buyer invoice stub: INV-2026-08-01-AZ-Contoso.pdf
- Requested outcomes: either reissue invoice with line-level allocations OR issue credit note(s) with corrected VAT math.

Please confirm receipt and provide an SLA/timeline — Contoso's accounting cutoff is 2026-08-15. If you need any additional format for the mapping, let us know.

Thanks,
Marcus Lin (on behalf of Redwood Inference)

Attachments: aug-billing-extract.csv, INV-2026-08-01-AZ-Contoso.pdf

Subject: RE: Fwd: Discrepancy: VAT charged and credits applied to wrong invoice — case 987654

Hi Marcus / Neha / Contoso team,

Thanks for all the detail and the attachments. Support case 987654 has been created. After initial ingestion and validation we can confirm:
1) The settlement file shows per-subscription credit metadata — however the Marketplace invoicing pipeline aggregated the settlement credit into a single invoice-level adjustment when rendering the buyer invoice.
2) This caused VAT to be calculated on pre-credit amounts for certain usage lines. We will: 
   - Reissue corrected invoice(s) with credits apportioned across the three subscription lines (INV-2026-08-01-R1), and
   - Issue an accompanying credit-note that addresses VAT recalculation where required.
3) Estimated ETA: draft corrected invoice to be available by 2026-08-20; final reissued PDF and credit notes by 2026-08-24.

Support case reference: 987654
Internal note: micro-billing team to adjust rendering pipeline for AggregatedCredits flag for Redwood seller id S-REDWOOD-332.

I've attached the case summary and our planned action. We'll add you to the case portal thread and share the reissued artifacts when ready.

Regards,
Priya Singh
Azure Marketplace Seller Support
seller-support@microsoft.com
